paragraphs: Rhinebeck Bancorp, Inc., (the "Company") a Maryland corporation, was incorporated in August 2018. On January 16, 2019, the Company became the holding company for Rhinebeck Bank (the "Bank") when it completed the reorganization of the Company and the Bank into a two-tier mutual holding company form of organization. The Company is regulated by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (the "Federal Reserve Board") and the New York State Department of Financial Services (the "NYSDFS"). The consolidated financial results contained herein reflect the consolidated accounts of the Company and the Bank.

At December 31, 2025, the Company had consolidated total assets of $1.30 billion, total deposits of $1.10 billion and stockholders' equity of $136.9 million. The Company's executive offices are located at 2 Jefferson Plaza, Poughkeepsie, New York 12601. The telephone number at this address is (845) 454-8555. Our website address is www.Rhinebeckbank.com. Information on this website is not and should not be considered a part of this report.

The Company files interim, quarterly and annual reports with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC"). The SEC maintains an Internet site (www.sec.gov) that contains reports, proxy and information statements and other information regarding issuers such as the Company that file electronically with the SEC. All filed SEC reports and interim filings can also be obtained from the Bank's website (www.Rhinebeckbank.com), on the "Investor Relations" page, without charge from Rhinebeck Bancorp, Inc.
Rhinebeck Bancorp, MHC, a New York-chartered non-stock corporation, is a mutual holding company that owns 57.0% of the outstanding common stock of Rhinebeck Bancorp, Inc.

On February 10, 2026, Rhinebeck Bancorp, MHC adopted a Plan of Conversion and Reorganization, pursuant to which Rhinebeck Bancorp, MHC is proposing to convert from the mutual holding company structure to the fully public stock holding company structure, in a transaction commonly referred to as a "second-step conversion." The second-step conversion requires the approval of the NYSDFS and the Federal Reserve Board, as well as the depositors of Rhinebeck Bank and the stockholders of the Company.

Rhinebeck Bank is a New York-chartered stock savings bank that was organized in 1860. We provide a full range of banking and financial services to consumer and commercial customers through our corporate office and 12 branches located in Dutchess, Orange and Ulster Counties. We also maintain a representative office in Albany County to originate indirect automobile and commercial loans and a representative office in Dutchess County for financial services. Financial services, including investment advisory and financial product sales, are offered through a division of the Bank doing business as Rhinebeck Asset Management ("RAM"). Our primary business activity is accepting deposits from the general public and using those funds together with borrowings, primarily to originate commercial real estate loans (which includes multi-family real estate loans and commercial construction loans), commercial business loans and indirect automobile loans (automobile loans referred to us by automobile dealerships) and to purchase one- to four-family residential real estate loans and investment securities.

We offer a variety of deposit accounts, including savings accounts, certificates of deposit, money market accounts, commercial and personal checking accounts and individual retirement accounts. We also offer alternative delivery channels, including ATMs, online banking and bill pay, mobile banking with mobile deposit and bill pay, Automated Clearing House origination, remote deposit capture and telephone banking.
We are subject to regulation and examination by the NYSDFS and by the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (the "FDIC").

Our primary market area encompasses Dutchess, Orange, Ulster and Albany Counties (and their contiguous counties), which are located in the Hudson Valley region of New York. Our retail banking offices (and the representative offices noted above) are located in these four counties and serve the surrounding areas. The Hudson Valley region has a diversified economy and representative industries include education, health, government, leisure and hospitality and professional business services. We view Orange and Albany Counties, which have larger populations than Dutchess and Ulster Counties, as primary areas for growth.

Based on published statistics, the U.S. unemployment rate was 4.4% as of December 31, 2025, while the New York State unemployment rate was 4.6%. The four counties in our primary market area each had a lower unemployment rate than New York State (Dutchess County, 3.2%, Orange County, 3.6%, Ulster County, 3.5% and Albany County, 3.3%). According to the New York State Department of Labor, for the twelve-month period ended December 31, 2025, the Hudson Valley's private sector job growth increased by 0.2%. Based on published statistics, median household income for 2024 (the latest date for which information was available) was $99,478 in Dutchess County, $97,178 in Orange County, $86,271 in Ulster County and $85,333 in Albany County, compared to $80,734 in the U.S. and $85,974 in New York State. Based on published statistics, the July 2024 estimated population was 299,963 in Dutchess County, 411,767 in Orange County, 182,977 in Ulster County and 319,964 in Albany County.

We face significant competition for deposits and loans. Our most direct competition for deposits has historically come from the numerous financial institutions operating in our market area (including other community and commercial banks, credit unions and financial technology companies), many of which are significantly larger than we are and have greater resources. We also face competition for investors' funds from other sources such as brokerage firms, money market funds and mutual funds, as well as securities, such as Treasury bills, offered by the Federal Government. Based on FDIC data, at June 30, 2025 (the latest date for which information is available), we had 10.44% of the FDIC-insured deposit market share in Dutchess County, which was fourth among the 15 institutions with offices in the county, 1.59% of the FDIC-insured deposit market share in Ulster County, which was 12th among the 18 institutions with offices in the county, and 1.28% of the FDIC-insured deposit market share in Orange County, which was 14th among the 22 institutions with offices in the county. In all three counties, New York City money center banks or large regional banks have a significant presence.

We expect competition to remain intense in the future as a result of legislative, regulatory and technological changes and the continuing trend of consolidation in the financial services industry. Technological advances, for example, have lowered barriers to entry, allowed banks to expand their geographic reach by providing services over the internet and made it possible for non-depository institutions, including financial technology companies, to offer products and services that traditionally have been provided by banks. Competition for deposits and the origination of loans could limit our growth in the future.

We seek to meet this competition with convenient branch locations and online offerings, emphasizing personalized banking and the advantage of local decision-making in our banking businesses. Specifically, we promote and maintain relationships and build customer loyalty within local communities by focusing our marketing and community involvement on the specific needs of individual neighborhoods. We do not rely on any individual, group, or entity for a material portion of our deposits.

Loans are our primary interest-earning asset. At December 31, 2025, net loans represented 73.2% of our total assets. Our allowance for credit losses, which primarily includes an allowance for credit losses on loans, is accounted for under the current expected credit loss ("CECL") model.

headings: Risks Related to Our Lending Activities
Our emphasis on commercial real estate and commercial business lending involves risks that could adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.
Our automobile loan portfolio exposes us to increased credit risks.
Our allowance for credit losses may not be sufficient to cover actual loan losses.
Our non-owner occupied commercial real estate loans may expose us to increased credit risk.
We are subject to environmental liability risk associated with lending activities.
Our business may be adversely affected by downturns in the local economy.

A decline in economic conditions could reduce demand for our products and services and/or result in increases in our level of non-performing loans, which could have an adverse effect on our results of operations.
Inflation can have an adverse impact on our business and on our customers.
Changes to trade policies and tariffs can have an adverse impact on our business and our customers.
Interruption of our customers' supply chains could negatively impact their business and operations and impact their ability to repay their loans.
Changes in interest rates may reduce our profits.
Risks Related to Our Funding and Liquidity

Our inability to generate core deposits may cause us to rely more heavily on wholesale funding strategies for funding and liquidity needs, which could have an adverse effect on our net interest margin and profitability.
A lack of liquidity could adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations and result in regulatory limits being placed on us.
Risk Related to Our Business Strategy
Our long-term business strategy involves organic growth, and our financial condition and results of operations may be adversely affected if we fail to grow or fail to manage our growth effectively.
Our inability to tailor our retail delivery model to respond to consumer preferences in banking may negatively affect earnings.
We may pursue acquisitions of other financial institutions, branch offices, lines of business, or lift-outs of lending or deposit gathering teams from other financial institutions.
Risks Related to Laws and Regulations
Changes in laws and regulations and the cost of regulatory compliance with new laws and regulations may adversely affect our operations and/or increase our costs of operations.
The fiscal, monetary and regulatory policies of the federal government and its agencies could have an adverse effect on our results of operations.
Non-compliance with the USA PATRIOT Act, Bank Secrecy Act, or other laws and regulations could result in fines or sanctions.
Changes in accounting standards could affect reported earnings.
We are subject to stringent capital requirements, which may adversely impact our return on equity, or constrain us from paying dividends or repurchasing shares.
Risks Related to Our Business and Operations
Strong competition within our market area may reduce our profits and slow growth.
Our cost of operations is high relative to our assets. Our failure to maintain or reduce our operating expenses may reduce our profits.
Our success depends on hiring and retaining certain key personnel.
Changes in management's estimates and assumptions may have a material impact on our consolidated financial statements and our financial condition or operating results.
We may be subject to risks and losses resulting from fraudulent activities that could adversely impact our financial performance and results of operations.
Our risk management framework may not be effective in mitigating risk and reducing the potential for significant losses.
We are a community bank and our ability to maintain our reputation is critical to the success of our business. The failure to do so may materially adversely affect our performance.
Risks Related to Our Wealth Management Business
Our wealth management business is subject to risks associated with the industry and strong competition for clients.
Risks Related to Privacy, Security and Technology

Regulations relating to privacy, information security and data protection could increase our costs, affect or limit how we collect and use personal information and adversely affect our business opportunities.
Systems failures or breaches of our network security could subject us to increased operating costs as well as litigation and other liabilities.
While our board of directors takes an active role in cybersecurity risk tolerance, we rely to a large degree on management and outside consultants in overseeing cybersecurity risk management.
Technological changes may adversely impact our business.
Risks Relating to Ownership of Our Common Stock
We may not pay any dividends on our common stock.
Our common stock is not heavily traded, and the stock price may fluctuate significantly.
The Company's Articles of Incorporation and Bylaws and Maryland law may discourage a corporate takeover.
paragraphs: In addition to factors discussed in the description of our business and elsewhere in this report, the following are factors that could adversely affect our future results of operations and financial condition.

We emphasize the origination of commercial real estate and commercial business loans. At December 31, 2025, our commercial real estate (which includes multi-family real estate loans and commercial construction loans) and commercial business loans totaled $626.3 million, or 65.4% of our loan portfolio. While these types of loans are potentially more profitable than residential mortgage loans due primarily to bearing generally higher interest rates and larger balances, they present greater risk due to greater dependency on the successful operation of the properties and are generally more sensitive to regional and local economic conditions, making future losses more difficult to predict. These loans also generally have relatively large balances to single borrowers or related groups of borrowers. Also, many of our borrowers have more than one of these types of loans outstanding. Consequently, an adverse development with respect to one loan or one credit relationship can expose us to a significantly greater risk of loss compared to an adverse development with respect to a residential mortgage loan. These loans also expose us to greater credit risk than loans secured by residential real estate because the collateral securing these loans typically cannot be liquidated as easily as residential real estate. If we foreclose on these loans, our holding period for the collateral typically is longer than for a single or multi-family residential property because there are fewer potential purchasers of the collateral. In addition, changes in consumer preferences about where they work, live, shop and eat can also impact commercial real estate, which could result in declines in occupancy and declines in property values. If loans that are collateralized by commercial real estate become troubled and the value of the real estate has been significantly impaired, then we may not be able to recover the full contractual amount of principal and interest that we anticipated at the time we originated the loan, which could cause us to increase our provision for credit losses and adversely affect our operating results and financial condition. Accordingly, any charge-offs may be larger on a per loan basis than those incurred with our residential or consumer loans. See "Item 1. Business — Loan Underwriting Risks."

At December 31, 2025, $213.8 million, or 22.3% of our total loan portfolio and 16.4% of our total assets, consisted of indirect automobile loans and $4.6 million, or 0.5% of our total loan portfolio, consisted of automobile loans that we also originated directly. Automobile loans are inherently risky as they are secured by assets that may be difficult to locate, have high loan-to-value ratios, and can depreciate rapidly. In some cases, repossessed collateral for a defaulted automobile loan may not provide an adequate source of repayment for the outstanding loan and the remaining deficiency may not warrant further collection efforts against the borrower. Automobile loan collections depend on the borrower's continuing financial stability, and therefore, are more likely to be adversely affected by job loss, divorce, illness, or personal bankruptcy. Furthermore, our consumer lending activities are subject to numerous consumer protection laws and regulations, and the application of various federal and state laws, including bankruptcy and insolvency laws, may limit our ability to recover on such loans. Additional risk elements associated with indirect lending include the limited personal contact with the borrower as a result of indirect lending through non-bank channels, namely automobile dealers, and reliance on automobile dealers to comply with fair lending practices. We also rely on dealerships to ensure our security interest in the financed vehicles is perfected. See "Item 1. Business — Loan Underwriting Risks."

We maintain an allowance for credit losses, which is established through a provision for credit losses that represents management's best estimate of the lifetime expected losses on loans. We make various assumptions and judgments about the collectability of loans in our portfolio, including the creditworthiness of borrowers, the strength of the economy and the value of the real estate, automobiles and other assets serving as collateral for the repayment of loans. In determining

the adequacy of the allowance for credit losses, we rely on our historic loss experience and our evaluation of economic conditions and other qualitative factors. If our assumptions prove to be incorrect, our allowance for credit losses may not be sufficient to cover losses inherent in our loan portfolio, and adjustments may be necessary.

The allowance for credit losses is dependent on various factors, including credit quality, macroeconomic forecasts and conditions, composition of our loans and securities portfolios, and other management judgements. There can be no assurance that our allowance for credit losses will be adequate to cover actual losses. In addition, federal and state regulators periodically review our allowance for credit losses and may require us to increase our provision for credit losses or recognize further loan charge-offs. Significant additions to the allowance could materially decrease our net income.

paragraphs: This discussion and analysis reflects information contained in our audited consolidated financial statements and other relevant statistical data, and is intended to enhance your understanding of our financial condition and results of operations. The information in this section has been derived from the audited consolidated financial statements contained within this Form 10-K.

Net Interest Income. Our primary source of income is net interest income. Net interest income is the difference between interest income, which is the income we earn on our loans and investments, and interest expense, which is the interest we pay on our deposits and borrowings.

Provision for Credit Losses on loans. The allowance for credit losses is a valuation allowance for the estimated lifetime credit losses. The allowance for credit losses is increased through charges to the provision for credit losses. Loans are charged against the allowance when management believes that the collectability of the principal loan amount is not probable. Recoveries on loans previously charged-off, if any, are credited to the allowance for credit losses when realized.

Non-interest Expenses. Our non-interest expenses consist of salaries and employee benefits, net occupancy and equipment, data processing, professional fees, marketing expenses, premium payments we make to the FDIC for insurance of our deposits and other general and administrative expenses.

Income Tax Expense. Our income tax expense is the total of the current year income tax due or refundable and the change in deferred tax assets and liabilities. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are the expected future tax amounts for the temporary differences between the carrying amounts and the tax basis of assets and liabilities, computed using enacted tax rates. A valuation allowance, if needed, reduces deferred tax assets to the amounts expected to be realized.

In October 2025, Matthew J. Smith was appointed President and Chief Executive Officer of Rhinebeck Bank and its holding companies, Rhinebeck Bancorp and Rhinebeck Bancorp, MHC, to lead Rhinebeck Bank into its next phase of growth and innovation. Mr. Smith's executive leadership experience includes overseeing community bank operations, spearheading the implementation of digital banking and banking-as-a-service programs and integrating acquired financial institutions. As we realign our strategies for growth, we intend to continue to operate as a well-capitalized and profitable community bank dedicated to providing exceptional personal service to our individual and business customers. We believe that we have a competitive advantage in the markets we serve because of our knowledge of the local marketplace and our long-standing history of providing superior, relationship-based customer service.

Our current business strategy includes the following key components, which are designed to improve earnings by expanding our net interest margin, increasing non-interest income and improving efficiency:

• Emphasize relationship-based commercial lending. Following the completion of our holding company reorganization and minority stock issuance in 2019, we began our expansion as a commercial lender. Our commercial real estate loan portfolio (which includes multi-family real estate and commercial construction loans) and commercial business loan portfolio have grown from $223.0 million and $83.2 million, or 32.9% and 12.2% of our total loan portfolio, respectively, at December 31, 2019 to $534.7 million and $91.5 million, or 55.8% and 9.5% of our total loan portfolio, respectively, at December 31, 2025. We believe that commercial real estate and commercial business lending offer opportunities to invest in our community, increase the overall yield earned on our loan portfolio and manage interest rate risk. We intend to continue to increase originations of these types of loans in our primary market area and may consider hiring additional lenders as well as originating loans secured by properties located in areas that are contiguous to our current market area.

Increasing our commercial real estate loans and commercial business loans involves risk, as described in "Risk Factors—Risks Related to Our Lending Activities—Our emphasis on commercial real estate and commercial business lending involves risks that could adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations" and "—Our non-owner occupied commercial real estate loans may expose us to increased credit risk."

• Grow and enhance our low-cost deposit base. Deposits are our primary source of funds for lending and investment. Core deposits, which we define as all non-time deposits, are a lower-cost and more stable source of funds than time deposits. We are making a concerted effort to increase these lower-cost transaction deposit accounts following a period of relatively higher interest rates during which customers migrated to higher-cost time deposits. As of December 31, 2025, core deposits totaled $720.4 million, or 65.6% of total deposits. We plan to continue to market our core transaction accounts, emphasizing our high-quality service and competitive pricing of these products.

We are also developing a full suite of treasury management services for business customers to encourage commercial borrowers to maintain deposit accounts with us and to generate recurring fee income. We view treasury management as a core strategic capability that will support both deposit growth and non-interest income diversification. We may also enter into strategic partnerships, including banking-as-a-service partnerships, to facilitate new account openings and provide a low-cost method to attract and retain core deposits.

• Invest in technology to improve efficiency and support scalable growth. We emphasize disciplined expense management to support sustainable profitability and operating leverage. We are investing in updated technology and digital capabilities to improve efficiency, enhance customer experience, and support scalable growth. We currently offer the convenience of certain technology-based products, such as mobile deposit capture, bill pay, card valet, and internet and mobile banking. We may invest in additional initiatives, including enhanced digital account opening, improved self-service capabilities, automation of

manual workflows, and selective use of advanced analytics to support operational efficiency and decision-making, including potential applications of artificial intelligence products. Management will monitor efficiency metrics relative to our peer institutions and aims to adjust our resource allocation to maintain competitiveness while preserving service quality.

• Increase household penetration and non-interest income through private banking services. We are focused on meeting the entire financial needs of our customer base by offering a full complement of banking solutions. Our customer relationships provide opportunities for cross-selling products to existing customers to deepen our "share of wallet." Further, we plan to explore establishing a private banking offering, designed as a relationship-led, advice-driven financial services model for mass-affluent and emerging-affluent individuals, business owners, professionals, and families whose needs exceed traditional retail banking but who are underserved or excluded by the high minimums and rigid structures of larger regional and national banks. Our existing wealth management business will serve as a natural complement to private banking offerings and provide an opportunity for household-level relationship expansion among both bank customers and wealth management clientele.

paragraphs: Rhinebeck Bancorp, Inc., (the "Company") 為一間馬裏蘭州公司，於2018年8月設立。於2019年1月16日，本公司完成公司與銀行的重組，成為Rhinebeck Bank (the "Bank") 的控股公司。本公司受美國聯邦儲備系統理事會 (the "Federal Reserve Board") 與紐約州財政服務局 (the "NYSDFS") 規範。本文件所包含的合併財務結果反映本公司與銀行的合併財務報表。
本公司向美國證券交易委員會 (the "SEC") 提交期中、季報與年報。SEC 保有網際網路網站 (www.sec.gov)，提供報告、股東權益書與資訊聲明及其他資訊，有關向 SEC 提交電子檔之發行者，例如本公司。所有提交至 SEC 之報告與期中檔亦可於銀行網站 (www.Rhinebeckbank.com) 的「投資人關係」頁面免費取得。
Rhinebeck Bancorp, MHC 為一間紐約州註冊之非營利公司，為一間相互制控股公司，持有Rhinebeck Bancorp, Inc. 57.0% 之發行普通股。
於2026年2月10日，Rhinebeck Bancorp, MHC 通過轉換與重組計畫，擬將本公司從相互制控股公司結構轉換為完全公開之股份控股公司結構，此交易常被稱為「第二步轉換」。第二步轉換需經NYSDFS 與美國聯邦儲備系統理事會批准，以及Rhinebeck Bank 之存款人與本公司之股東同意。

Rhinebeck Bank 為一間紐約州註冊之股份儲蓄銀行，於1860年設立。我們透過總部與設於杜赫斯、奧蘭治與烏爾斯特縣之12家分行，為消費者與企業客戶提供全方位之銀行與金融服務。我們亦於阿爾巴尼縣設有代表處，用以發放間接汽車貸款與商業貸款，並於杜赫斯縣設有代表處提供金融服務。投資顧問與金融產品銷售等金融服務，則透過銀行之分公司Rhinebeck Asset Management ("RAM") 提供。本公司主要業務為接受公眾存款，並與借入資金共同用以發放商業不動產貸款 (包括多戶住宅不動產貸款與商業建設貸款)、商業企業貸款與間接汽車貸款 (由汽車經銷商轉介之汽車貸款)，以及購買一至四戶住宅不動產貸款與投資證券。
我們提供多種存款帳戶，包括儲蓄帳戶、定期存款、貨幣市場帳戶、商業與個人支票帳戶及個人退休帳戶。我們亦提供多元服務管道，包括ATM、網際網路銀行與付款、行動銀行與行動存款及付款、自動清算系統貸款、遠端存款與電話銀行。
本公司受紐約州財政服務局與美國存款保險公司 (the "FDIC") 規範與檢查。

本公司主要服務區域為 Dutchess、Orange、Ulster 與 Albany 縣（及其毗鄰縣市），這些縣市位於紐約州的 Hudson Valley 區域。本公司零售銀行分行（以及上述代表辦事處）位於這四個縣市，並服務周邊地區。Hudson Valley 區域經濟結構多元，代表性產業包括教育、醫療、政府、休閒與餐飲以及專業商業服務。本公司視 Orange 與 Albany 縣為主要成長區域，因這兩個縣的人口較 Dutchess 與 Ulster 縣為多。

根據公佈的統計資料，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，美國失業率為 4.4%，紐約州失業率為 4.6%。本公司主要服務區域的四個縣市，其失業率均低於紐約州（Dutchess 縣 3.2%，Orange 縣 3.6%，Ulster 縣 3.5%，Albany 縣 3.3%）。根據紐約州勞工部資料，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日的十二個月期間，Hudson Valley 私營部門就業人數成長 0.2%。根據公佈的統計資料，2024 年（最新資料為 2024 年）的中位數家庭收入為：Dutchess 縣為 99,478 美元，Orange 縣為 97,178 美元，Ulster 縣為 86,271 美元，Albany 縣為 85,333 美元，較美國的 80,734 美元與紐約州的 85,974 美元為高。根據公佈的統計資料，2024 年 7 月預估人口為：Dutchess 縣為 299,963 人，Orange 縣為 411,767 人，Ulster 縣為 182,977 人，Albany 縣為 319,964 人。

我們在存款與貸款業務方面面臨著顯著的競爭。我們在存款業務的主要競爭對手為市場內眾多的金融機構（包括其他社區與商業銀行、信用合作社及金融科技公司），其中許多機構規模遠大於我們，且擁有更多資源。我們也從其他來源面臨投資人資金的競爭，例如證券經紀商、貨幣市場基金與共同基金，以及美國聯邦政府所提供的國庫券等證券。根據 FDIC 資料，截至 2025 年 6 月 30 日（最新資料為 2025 年 6 月 30 日），我們在 Dutchess 縣的 FDIC 保險存款市場佔有率為 10.44%，為該縣 15 家設有辦事處機構中排名第四；在 Ulster 縣的 FDIC 保險存款市場佔有率為 1.59%，為該縣 18 家設有辦事處機構中排名第 12；在 Orange 縣的 FDIC 保險存款市場佔有率為 1.28%，為該縣 22 家設有辦事處機構中排名第 14。在這三個縣市中，紐約市的錢中心銀行或大型區域銀行均有顯著的影響力。
我們預期未來競爭將持續激烈，這是因為立法、監管與科技變革，以及金融服務業持續合併的趨勢所致。例如，科技進步已降低進入門檻，使銀行能透過網際網路拓展地理範圍，並讓非存款機構（包括金融科技公司）提供以往由銀行提供的產品與服務。存款與貸款業務的競爭可能限制我們未來的成長。
我們透過便利的分行位置與線上服務來應對競爭，強調個性化銀行服務與本地決策優勢。具體而言，我們透過聚焦個別社區的特定需求，來促進與維持關係並建立客戶忠誠度。我們的行銷與社區參與均著重於個別社區的特定需求。我們不依賴任何個人、團體或機構來取得我們存款的大部分。
貸款為我們主要的獲利資產。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，淨貸款佔我們總資產的 73.2%。我們的信用損失撥備（主要包含貸款信用損失撥備）依照當前預期信用損失（"CECL"）模型進行會計處理。

paragraphs: 本討論與分析反映本行經審計之合併財務報表及其他相關統計資料，並旨在增進您對本行財務狀況與營運成果之理解。本節資料係根據本表單 10-K 所含之經審計合併財務報表所衍生。
淨利息收入。本行主要收入來源為淨利息收入。淨利息收入係指利息收入（即本行於貸款與投資所賺取之收入）與利息支出（即本行於存款與借款所支付之利息）之差額。
貸款信用減損準備。信用減損準備係用以評估貸款之預期終身信用減損之價值減損準備。信用減損準備透過信用減損準備費用之計提而增加。貸款於管理層認為貸款本金之可收回性不具備時，將直接核銷信用減損準備。若已核銷貸款後有回復，則於實現時將回復金額計入信用減損準備。
非利息支出。本行之非利息支出包含薪資與員工福利、淨營業與設備支出、資料處理、專業費用、行銷費用、我們支付給 FDIC 用以保險存款之 premiums，以及其他一般及行政費用。
所得稅費用。本行之所得稅費用係指當年度應繳或可退回之所得稅，以及遞延所得稅資產與負債之變動。遞延所得稅資產與負債係指資產與負債帳面價值與稅基之間之暫時差異所產生之未來稅務金額，係以已公告之稅率計算。若需，則遞延所得稅資產之價值減損準備將遞延所得稅資產減至預期可實現之金額。

2025 年 10 月，Matthew J. Smith 被任命為 Rhinebeck Bank 及其控股公司 Rhinebeck Bancorp 與 Rhinebeck Bancorp, MHC 之董事長與首席執行官，以領導 Rhinebeck Bank 進入其下一個成長與創新階段。Mr. Smith 之執行領導經驗包含 oversee 社區銀行營運、推動數位銀行與銀行即服務（banking-as-a-service）計畫之實施，以及整合收購之金融機構。隨著我們重新調整成長策略，我們意圖持續運作為一家資本充足且獲利之社區銀行，致力於為個人與企業客戶提供卓越之個人服務。我們相信，我們在所服務市場中擁有競爭優勢，因我們對當地市場之瞭解，以及我們長期提供優質、基於關係之客戶服務之歷史。
我們目前之業務策略包含以下關鍵零組件，旨在透過擴大淨利息邊際、增加非利息收入與提升效率來改善獲利：

• 強調基於關係之商業貸款。在 2019 年完成控股公司重組與少數股發行後，我們開始以商業貸款之方式進行擴張。我們之商業不動產貸款組合（包含多戶住宅不動產與商業建設貸款）與商業企業貸款組合，已從 2019 年 12 月 31 日之 223.0 百萬美元與 83.2 百萬美元，或佔總貸款組合之 32.9% 與 12.2%，成長至 2025 年 12 月 31 日之 534.7 百萬美元與 91.5 百萬美元，或佔總貸款組合之 55.8% 與 9.5%。我們認為，商業不動產與商業企業貸款提供機會投資於我們之社區，提高貸款組合之總收益率，並管理利率風險。我們意圖持續在主要市場區增加這些類型貸款之放款，並可能考慮聘請更多貸款員，以及放款以位於目前市場區周邊地區之不動產為擔保之貸款。
增加我們的商業不動產貸款及商業企業貸款涉及風險，如 "風險因素—與我們的貸款活動相關的風險—我們對商業不動產及商業企業貸款的重視可能導致對我們財務狀況及營運結果產生不利影響" 以及 "—我們的非自用商業不動產貸款可能使我們面臨更高的信用風險。"

• 擴大並強化我們的低成本存款基礎。存款是我們貸款及投資的主要資金來源。我們將核心存款定義為所有非定期存款，這是較低成本且更穩定的資金來源，相比定期存款而言。我們正在努力增加這些低成本交易存款帳戶，因應過去一段較高利率時期，客戶轉向較高成本的定期存款。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，核心存款總計為 720.4 百萬美元，佔總存款的 65.6%。我們計畫持續行銷我們的核心交易帳戶，強調我們高品質的服務及這些產品的競爭性價格。
我們同時也在開發一套完整的企業客戶財務管理服務，以鼓勵商業借款人維持與我們的存款帳戶，並產生持續的費用收入。我們將財務管理視為核心戰略能力，將支持存款成長及非利息收入的多元化。我們也可能與策略性夥伴，包括銀行即服務夥伴，合作，以促進新帳戶開設，並提供一種低成本的方法來吸引及保留核心存款。
• 投資於科技以提高效率並支持可擴展的成長。我們強調嚴謹的費用管理，以支持可持續的獲利及營運槓桿。我們正在投資更新的科技及數位能力，以提高效率、增強客戶體驗，並支持可擴展的成長。我們目前提供某些基於科技的產品便利性，例如行動存款、付款、卡片管理、網際網路及行動銀行。我們可能投資於其他計畫，包括增強的數位帳戶開設、改善的自助服務能力、自動化
手動作業流程，以及選擇性使用先進分析，以支持作業效率及決策，包括潛在應用的人工智慧產品。管理層將監測效率指標與我們同業機構的比較，並旨在調整我們的資源配置，以維持競爭力同時維護服務品質。

• 透過私人銀行服務提高家庭滲透率及非利息收入。我們專注於透過提供完整的銀行解決方案來滿足客戶的全部金融需求。我們的客戶關係為我們提供機會，向現有客戶交叉銷售產品，以深化我們的 "客戶消費比例"。此外，我們計畫探討建立私人銀行服務，設計為以關係為導向、以建議為驅動的金融服務模式，服務大眾富裕及新興富裕個人、企業主、專業人士及家庭，其需求超過傳統零售銀行，但卻被較大區域及國家銀行的高最低金額及僵化結構所排除。我們現有的資產管理業務將作為私人銀行服務的自然補充，並提供機會在銀行客戶及資產管理客戶之間進行家庭層級的關係擴張。

headings: 與我們貸款業務相關的風險
我們對商業不動產及商業營運貸款的重視，可能導致對我們財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
我們的汽車貸款組合使我們面臨更高的信用風險。
我們的信用損失撥備可能無法足夠覆蓋實際的貸款損失。
我們的非自用商業不動產貸款可能使我們面臨更高的信用風險。
我們因貸款業務而面臨環境責任風險。
與總體經濟狀況相關的風險
我們的業務可能因當地經濟衰退而受到不利影響。
經濟條件惡化可能降低對我們產品與服務的需求，並/或導致我們非 Performing Loans 水準增加，這可能會對我們營運成果產生不利影響。
通貨膨脹可能對我們的業務及客戶產生不利影響。
貿易政策與關稅的變動可能對我們的業務及客戶產生不利影響。
客戶供應鏈中斷可能對其業務與營運產生負面影響，並影響其償還貸款的能力。
利率變動可能降低我們的利潤。
與我們資金與流動性相關的風險
我們若無法產生核心存款，可能需更依賴 Wholesale Funding 策略來滿足資金與流動性需求，這可能會對我們的淨利息-margin 及利潤產生不利影響。
流動性不足可能會不利影響本公司的財務狀況及營運結果，並導致 regulators 對本公司設置監管限制。
與本公司商業策略相關之風險
本公司長期商業策略涉及內生性成長，若本公司未能成長或未能有效管理成長，可能會不利影響財務狀況及營運結果。
本公司若無法調整零售交付模式以回應銀行業消費者的偏好，可能會不利影響營收。
本公司可能進行收購其他金融機構、分行、業務線，或從其他金融機構分拆貸款或存款集結團隊。
與法律及法規相關之風險
法律及法規之變更，以及遵守新法律及法規之成本，可能會不利影響營運及/或增加營運成本。
美國聯邦政府及其機構的財政、貨幣及法規政策，可能會對本公司營運結果產生不利影響。
未遵守美國反恐協調法、銀行保密法或其他法律法規，可能會導致處罰或制裁。
會計準則的變更可能影響所報告的獲利。
我們需遵守嚴格的資本要求，這可能會不利於我們的權益回報率，或限制我們支付股息或買回股票的能力。
與我們業務及營運相關的風險
我們所處市場區域內的強烈競爭可能會降低我們的利潤並減緩成長速度。
我們的營運成本相對於資產而言偏高。我們若無法維持或降低營運費用，可能會減少我們的利潤。
我們的成功取決於聘僱及留住某些關鍵人員。
管理階層對會計估計與假設的變更，可能對我們合併財務報表及財務狀況或營運成果產生重大影響。
我們可能面臨因詐欺活動而產生的風險與損失，這可能會對我們的財務表現及營運結果造成不利影響。
我們的風險管理架構可能無法有效降低風險並減少產生重大損失的潛在可能性。
我們是一家社區銀行，維護我們的聲譽對我們業務的成功至關重要。若未能做到，可能會對我們的表現造成重大不利影響。
與我們資產管理業務相關的風險
我們的資產管理業務面臨與產業相關的風險以及客戶競爭激烈的挑戰。
與隱私權、安全及科技相關的風險
與隱私權、資訊安全及資料保護相關的法規可能會增加我們的成本，影響或限制我們收集及使用個人資料的方式，並對我們的業務機會產生不利影響。
系統故障或我們網路安全遭入侵的情況，可能會使我們面臨更高的營運成本以及訴訟及其他責任。
雖然我們的董事會積極參與網路安全風險容忍度的評估，但我們在監督網路安全風險管理方面很大程度上依賴管理層及外部顧問。
科技變革可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。
與本公司普通股 ownership 相關的風險
我們可能不會就本公司普通股支付任何股息。
本公司普通股並未大量交易，且股票價格可能大幅波動。
本公司章程及規章與馬裏蘭州法律可能阻卻公司收購案的發生。
paragraphs: 除本報告中於業務說明及其他地方所討論的因素外，以下為可能對我們未來營運結果及財務狀況產生不利影響的因素。

我們強調商業不動產及商業貸款的發放。於2025年12月31日，我們的商業不動產（包含多戶住宅不動產貸款及商業建築貸款）及商業貸款總計為626.3 百萬美元，佔我們貸款組合的65.4%。雖然這些貸款類型由於主要承擔較高的利率及較大的貸款餘額，潛在上可能比住宅抵押貸款更具利潤性，但它們因更依賴於不動產成功運作，而面臨較高的風險，且通常對區域及地方經濟條件較為敏感，使未來虧損更難預測。這些貸款通常對單一借款人或相關借款人集團具有相對較大的貸款餘額。此外，我們許多借款人同時持有這些類型的貸款。因此，針對某一貸款或某一信用關係的不利發展，可能會使我們面臨較住宅抵押貸款更高的損失風險。這些貸款也比以住宅不動產為擔保的貸款具有更高的信用風險，因為擔保這些貸款的抵押品通常較難迅速變現。若我們對這些貸款進行拍賣，我們持有抵押品的期間通常會比單一或多戶住宅不動產更長，因為抵押品的潛在買家較少。此外，消費者對工作、居住、購物及用餐地點的偏好變化，也可能影響商業不動產，這可能會導致租賃率下降及不動產價值下跌。若以商業不動產為擔保的貸款出現問題，且不動產價值已顯著減損，我們可能無法回收貸款發放時預期的全部本金及利息，這可能會導致我們增加信貸損失備抵，並對我們的營運成果及財務狀況產生負面影響。因此，針對每一筆貸款的核銷金額，可能會比我們的住宅或消費貸款更高。請參閱「項目1.業務—貸款授信風險」。

於2025年12月31日，我們總貸款組合的22.3%及總資產的16.4%為間接汽車貸款，總計為213.8 百萬美元，而我們直接發放的汽車貸款總計為4.6 百萬美元，佔總貸款組合的0.5%。汽車貸款本質上風險較高，因其擔保品可能難以尋獲、貸款價值比率較高，且價值可能迅速 depreciate。在某些情況下， defaulted 汽車貸款的抵質品可能無法提供足夠的償還來源，且剩餘的虧損可能不值得進一步對借款人進行追討。汽車貸款的回收取決於借款人的持續財務穩定，因此，較容易受到失業、離婚、疾病或個人破產的影響。此外，我們的消費貸款業務受到眾多消費者保護法規的規範，而各項聯邦及州法律，包括破產及無力償債法，可能限制我們對這些貸款的回收能力。與間接貸款相關的其他風險因素包括因透過非銀行渠道（即汽車經銷商）進行貸款，導致與借款人之間的個人接觸有限，以及依賴汽車經銷商遵守公平貸款實踐。我們也依賴經銷商確保我們對貸款汽車的擔保權益已完全確立。請參閱「項目1.業務—貸款授信風險」。
我們維持信用損失備抵，該備抵透過信用損失備抵費用建立，代表管理層對貸款組閤中貸款未來預期損失的最佳估計。我們對貸款組閤中貸款的可收回性做出各種假設與判斷，包括借款人的信用狀況、經濟狀況及擔保品（如不動產、汽車及其他資產）的價值。
在評估信用損失備抵是否充足時，我們依賴我們的歷史損失經驗及對經濟狀況及其他質性因素的評估。若我們的假設證明錯誤，則信用損失備抵可能不足以覆蓋貸款組閤中內在的損失，且可能需要進行調整。
信用損失備抵取決於多種因素，包括信用品質、總體經濟預測及狀況、貸款及證券組合的組成，以及其他管理層判斷。無法保證信用損失備抵將足以覆蓋實際損失。此外，聯邦及州監管機構會定期審查我們的信用損失備抵，並可能要求我們增加信用損失備抵費用或承認進一步的貸款核銷。信用損失備抵的重大增加可能對我們的淨收入造成重大影響。
